title: Capstone: Architecting a Well-Architected Web Application

questions.prompt: Order the components a dynamic web request passes through, from the user to the data.
questions.explanation: The request resolves DNS (Route 53), hits the CDN (CloudFront), reaches the load balancer (ALB), routes to a stateless app server (ASG), which reads/writes the private data tier.

questions.prompt: Why must the application tier be stateless in this architecture?

options.text: So any instance can serve any request and the Auto Scaling group can add or replace instances freely
Because AWS forbids storing any data
To make the servers run faster CPUs
It has no effect on the design

questions.explanation: Stateless servers let the load balancer and Auto Scaling group route to, add, or replace any instance; session state lives in ElastiCache/DynamoDB instead of on a server.

questions.prompt: How does the design survive an Availability Zone failure?

options.text: It runs in a single AZ and simply restarts
It spans multiple AZs, so the ALB routes to healthy servers, RDS Multi-AZ fails over, and the ASG rebuilds capacity
It cannot survive an AZ failure

questions.explanation: Multi-AZ redundancy plus self-healing (ELB health checks, RDS Multi-AZ failover, ASG replacement) turns an AZ outage into a non-event.

questions.prompt: Match each design choice to the Well-Architected pillar it best serves.
questions.explanation: IaC serves operational excellence, identity/encryption/secrets serve security, multi-AZ and self-healing serve reliability, and commitments/right-sizing serve cost optimization.

questions.prompt: How is background work (like sending email) kept from slowing the user's request?

options.text: It is decoupled onto SQS/SNS and processed asynchronously by Lambda
The user must wait for it to finish
It runs on the DNS server

questions.explanation: Queuing async work to SQS/SNS and processing it with Lambda lets the request return immediately while the work happens in the background.

questions.prompt: What makes a design 'well-architected' rather than merely working? Select all that apply.

options.text: Redundancy across multiple AZs for reliability
Security layers: least-privilege IAM, encryption, private subnets
A single instance with a hardcoded password and a public bucket

questions.explanation: Well-architected means deliberate choices across the pillars — reliability, security, operations, and cost. A single-AZ, hardcoded-secret, public-bucket design fails those pillars even if it runs.
